blanks.sentence: Alicia worried that lower-income people struggled to afford a _____.
Poor diets may lead to earlier _____ among people in poverty.
Many people lacked cooking knowledge and could not afford to _____ with ingredients.
The programme first sends all the necessary _____ to people’s homes.
The project assumes that real _____ begins at home.
Each online group includes a _____ who gives practical cooking advice.
Participants are encouraged to cook the first recipe by _____.
The onion-cutting method impressed Ally because of its neatness and _____.
Ally would use less chilli next time because her husband likes a lot of _____.
Being heavy-handed with an ingredient means using _____ of it.

multipleChoice.question: What problem creates the context for the project?
options: People have stopped shopping for food completely.
Rising food prices make shopping difficult for some people.
Restaurants have become cheaper than home cooking.
The UK is the only place where food prices have risen.

multipleChoice.question: What is the main purpose of Bags of Taste?
options: To sell restaurant meals to twelve customers each night.
To teach people only how to use social media.
To replace supermarkets with online cooking groups.
To help people eat better while spending less on food.

multipleChoice.question: What claim does Alicia make about diet in the UK?
options: Diet is a major driver of unequal health outcomes.
Diet has little connection with poverty.
Poorer people usually have the best diets.
Young people become healthier because of poverty.

multipleChoice.question: What practical barrier did Alicia identify?
options: People refused to eat meals they already liked.
People had too many free ingredients to test.
People lacked cooking confidence and could not risk wasting food.
People found all healthy meals quick and cheap.

multipleChoice.question: Why does the programme deliver ingredients to people’s homes?
options: To stop participants from cooking at home.
To make behaviour change practical in the home environment.
To test whether restaurants can deliver faster.
To avoid giving people any recipes.

multipleChoice.question: What role does the WhatsApp mentor play?
options: Providing cooking guidance and practical suggestions.
Judging participants in a formal competition.
Charging extra money for every recipe.
Replacing all interaction with videos only.

multipleChoice.question: Why is the onion-cutting video mentioned?
options: To show that participants must avoid onions.
To prove chana masala is impossible to cook.
To advertise a restaurant’s professional recipe.
To show how the project removes a small cooking difficulty.

multipleChoice.question: How does Ally respond to the onion-cutting method?
options: She thinks it is confusing and not worth using.
She says it makes the dish too spicy.
She finds it positive, tidy and easy to follow.
She refuses to try it until the next recipe.

multipleChoice.question: What does Ally’s comment suggest about her cooking experience?
options: She reflected on the result and would adjust the seasoning next time.
She decided never to cook chana masala again.
She believed the recipe contained no chilli at all.
She thought the mentor had forbidden spicy food.

multipleChoice.question: What overall benefit of Bags of Taste is highlighted near the end?
options: It makes restaurant dining affordable for everyone.
It combines cooking skills, healthier eating and lower cost.
It removes the need for participants to buy food forever.
It focuses mainly on expensive meals for special occasions.
